title: Relative finite presentation lifts over a square-zero base for a base-flat algebra
statement: Let $R\to A\to C$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings with the indicated composite $R\to C$, and let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal with $I^2=0$. Write $IA\subseteq A$ and $IC\subseteq C$ for the ideals generated by its images. Assume that $C$ is flat as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then $A\to C$ is of finite presentation if and only if $A/IA\to C/IC$ is of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. No flatness of $A$ over $R$, finite-generation of $I$, or Noetherian assumption is made.

source.place: Tag 06AG (lemma-deform-property), proof of clause (13), affine diagram in general remark (I), generator lifting from clause (11), and the displayed polynomial-kernel argument. Specialize the base to Spec R and the affine target/source to Spec A and Spec C.

proof.text: First suppose $C\cong A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Reducing coefficients gives $C/IC\cong (A/IA)[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(\bar f_1,\ldots,\bar f_m)$: both sides are $A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/((f_1,\ldots,f_m)+IA[x_1,\ldots,x_n])$. Indeed coefficient reduction is surjective with kernel the polynomials whose coefficients lie in $IA$, by [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. This proves the forward implication, without flatness.

source.place: Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property, proof of clause (13), using clause (11) and general remark (I)

proof.text:
Conversely, choose finite algebra generators of $ ar C=C/IC$ over $ ar A=A/IA$ from its finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and lift them to $c_1,\ldots,c_n\in C$. Put $P=A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and let $q:P	o C$ evaluate $x_j$ at $c_j$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Its image $D$ satisfies $C=D+IC$. For $c\in C$, write $c=d+\sum i_
u c_
u$ with $i_
u\in I$, then $c_
u=d_
u+e_
u$ with $e_
u\in IC$. Since $I^2=0$, $c=d+\sum i_
u d_
u\in D$. Thus $q$ is surjective. All sums here are finite; no finite generation of $I$ is used.

source.place: Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property, proof of clause (13), using clause (11) and general remark (I)

proof.text: For any $R$-module $M$, the balanced formulas $\bar r\otimes m\mapsto rm\bmod IM$ and $m\bmod IM\mapsto\bar1\otimes m$ are inverse maps $(R/I)\otimes_R M\cong M/IM$. They are well-defined because $I$ kills both targets, and are inverse on tensor generators [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. These maps commute with every $R$-linear map, by evaluating on $\bar r\otimes m$. In particular they apply to $K=\ker q$, $P$, and $C$. Coefficient reduction identifies $P/IP$ with $\bar A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring].

source.place: Tag 06AG, lemma-deform-property, proof of clause (13), using clause (11) and general remark (I)

proof.text: The sequence $0\to K\to P\xrightarrow{q}C\to0$ is short exact as $R$-modules. Its last term is flat over $R$ by hypothesis, so [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective], with tensor factor $R/I$, makes its tensor sequence short exact. Under the natural identifications in Step 3 this reads $0\to K/IK\to\bar A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\xrightarrow{\bar q}\bar C\to0$. Thus $K/IK$ identifies with the actual ideal $\ker\bar q$. The maps respect the $P$-action (on tensors the action is on the second factor), so this identification is an isomorphism of $P/IP$-modules. No flatness of $P$ or $A$ was invoked.

source.place: Tag 00HL, lemma-flat-tor-zero; applied as in Tag 06AG, clause (13)

proof.text: The map $\bar q$ is a surjection from a polynomial ring in finitely many variables, and $\bar C$ is finitely presented over $\bar A$ by assumption. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-surjection-kernel-fg] says its kernel is finitely generated. Lift a finite generating list through the surjection $K\to K/IK=\ker\bar q$, obtaining $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in K$. Let $L=(f_1,\ldots,f_m)\subseteq P$. Lifting the polynomial coefficients of any linear combination of their reduced classes gives $K=L+IK$.

source.place: Tag 00R2, lemma-finite-presentation-independent; used in Tag 06AG, clause (13)

proof.text: Substitute $K=L+IK$ once more: $K=L+I(L+IK)=L+IL+I^2K=L$, since $IL\subseteq L$ and $I^2=0$. This is the square-zero case of the nilpotent Nakayama argument, written out without any finiteness assumption on $K$. Therefore the surjective map $q$ has kernel $(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$ and gives $C\cong A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$. By [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], $C$ is finitely presented over $A$. Empty lists and the zero ring are allowed throughout.
